info.title: Autoxide API
info.description:
REST API of Autoxide.

## Conventions

Every endpoint follows the same rules, so learning one endpoint teaches all of them.

- **Success**: a single result is `{"data": …}`; a list is `{"data": […], "pagination": {"limit", "next_cursor"}}`. Creating a record answers `201` with a `Location` header pointing to it.
- **Errors**: always RFC 9457 Problem Details (`application/problem+json`). Branch on the stable `code` field, never on `detail`. Validation problems list every invalid field of the request in `errors`, all at once.
- **Lists**: accept `limit` (1–200, default 50), `order` (`desc` or `asc`, by creation time) and `cursor`. Some lists also take `sort` to order by another field, and their own filters. To get the next page, pass `pagination.next_cursor` as `cursor` with the same `order`, `sort` and filters; `null` means last page.
- **Authentication**: endpoints that need it list the `bearer` security scheme. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. A `401` response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`; its `code` says whether the token is missing, invalid or expired. Public endpoints list an empty requirement next to `bearer`: they work without a token, and a sent token must still be valid.
- **Retries**: send `Idempotency-Key: <a random UUID>` with `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE`. Repeating the same request with the same key within 24 hours returns the first result (marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of doing it twice; a different request with a used key gets `422`, and a repeat while the first is still running gets `409`.
- **Concurrent edits**: reading a single record returns its version in `ETag`. Send it back in `If-Match` when changing the record: if someone changed it in between, the answer is `412` (code `precondition_failed`) instead of silently overwriting their change. Without `If-Match` the change is made anyway, except on endpoints that say `If-Match` is required: those answer `428` (code `precondition_required`).
- **Caching**: send the `ETag` you have in `If-None-Match` when reading again; if nothing changed the answer is `304 Not Modified` with no body.
- **Deprecation**: an endpoint being retired is marked `deprecated` here and answers with `Deprecation` (RFC 9745), `Sunset` (RFC 8594, the removal date) and `Link: <…>; rel="successor-version"` headers. Move to the successor before the sunset date.
- **Language**: send `Accept-Language` (e.g. `vi`) to get the `detail` of errors in that language; English (`en`) by default and for unsupported languages. Responses carry `Content-Language`. Codes never change with the language.
- **Rate limits**: too many requests from one address are answered with `429` (code `rate_limited`) and a `Retry-After` header giving the seconds to wait.
- **Request id**: every response carries `x-request-id`. Send your own to correlate calls; quote it when reporting a problem.
- **IDs** are UUIDv7 strings; **timestamps** are UTC in RFC 3339; **money** is an integer amount in the smallest currency unit plus a currency code.

get.summary: See what the AI features can do.
get.description:
Requires `ai.view`. Tells whether text generation and embeddings are on, the provider and
models, whether images are read, and today's token use against the daily limit. Use it to
show or hide AI actions in a user interface. The operator turns AI on with the
`AUTOXIDE_AI_*` and `AUTOXIDE_EMBEDDING_*` settings.

post.summary: Confirm an email address with the token from a verification mail.
post.description:
Needs no sign-in: the token proves the mail was received. When the token was sent
for a new address (`POST /api/v1/auth/me/email`), the account's email becomes that
address; sign in with it from now on. Every other verification token of the
account stops working.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Language of the `detail` of errors: `en` (the default) or `vi`. Codes never change with the language.

200.description: Verified; the account as it is now.

400.description: The token is unknown, expired or used; code `auth.invalid_verification_token`.

409.description: Another account took this address meanwhile; code `auth.email_taken`.

422.description: The body is missing a field or a value is invalid.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password.
post.description:
Returns a short-lived access token and a refresh token. When the account has
two-step sign-in on, answers 202 instead: send the `mfa_token` and a code to
`POST /api/v1/auth/login/mfa`. The same error answers an unknown email and a
wrong password. After several failed attempts the email is locked for a while,
even for the right password.

parameters.description: Language of the `detail` of errors: `en` (the default) or `vi`. Codes never change with the language.

401.description: Wrong email or password; code `auth.invalid_credentials`.

422.description: The body is missing a field or a value is invalid.

429.description: Too many failed sign-ins for this email; code `auth.login_throttled`. Wait the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Finish signing in with a code from the authenticator app or a recovery code.
post.description:
Send the `mfa_token` from `POST /api/v1/auth/login` within its `expires_in`
seconds. Each `mfa_token` allows five wrong codes; wrong codes also count
towards the sign-in lock of the email.

itself, so no two-step code is asked for.

This cannot be undone: download your data first with `GET /api/v1/auth/me/export`.

page_url.description: Page the form was sent from.

referrer.description: Page that led the sender to the form, when the website sends it.

spam_reason.description:
Why the anti-spam checks held it (`too_fast`, `duplicate`, `classifier`…, joined by
commas); `null` unless `spam`.

SubmissionStatus.description: Where a submission is in the inbox.

SubmitRequest.description: A submission of a public form.

challenge.description: The value of the `altcha` widget, when the server uses a challenge.

data.description:
Answers by field key: a string for most types, a number for `number`, an array of
option values for `checkbox`, `true` for a ticked `consent`. Omit (or send `""` /
`null`) unanswered fields. Unknown keys are refused.

form_token.description:
Token from `GET /api/v1/antispam/token?scope=forms:<key>`; needed unless the caller
has the permission `forms.submit` (a website server with its own API key). Being
signed in without it is not enough.

locale.description: Language the form was shown in: `en` or `vi`.

page_url.description: Address of the page the form is on; omitted: the `Referer` header.

referrer.description: Page that led the visitor there (`document.referrer`), if any.

trap.description: The hidden trap field: people leave it empty.

id.description: Id of the submission. Sending the same form token again returns the same id.

message.description: The form's success message, in the language sent.

challenge.description: The value of the `altcha` widget, when the server uses a challenge.

consent_text.description: The exact consent text shown next to the form (kept as proof), up to 2000 characters.

consent_version.description: Version of that text, if you keep versions.

form_token.description:
Token from `GET /api/v1/antispam/token?scope=newsletter:subscribe`; needed unless the
caller has the permission `newsletter.subscribe` (a website server with its own API
key). Being signed in without it is not enough.

locale.description: Language of the confirmation mail: `en` or `vi`.

name.description: Up to 200 characters. Never put in the confirmation mail.

source.description: Where the form is (kept with the consent), e.g. `footer`; up to 100 characters.

trap.description: The hidden trap field: people leave it empty.

SubscribeResponse.description: The answer to a sign-up: always the same.

accepted.description: Always `true`. Tell the visitor to check their inbox if a list needs confirming.

email.description: In lower case.

soft_bounces.description: Soft bounces since the address was last taken off the suppression list.

suppressed.description:
Why the address is on the suppression list (`hard_bounce`, `soft_bounce`, `complaint`,
`manual`); `null`: it is not.

SubscriberStatus.description: Whether a subscriber may get mail at all.

SubscriptionResponse.description: A subscription of a subscriber to one list.

consent.description: Proof of consent: `{text, version, at, source, ip_fingerprint}` as recorded.

hold_reason.description: Why the anti-spam checks held the sign-up (it then needed confirming by mail).

SubscriptionStatus.description: Where a subscriber stands on one list.

SuppressionResponse.description: An address that gets no campaign mail.

note.description: A note, or the SMTP code of a bounce.

TagResponse.description: A tag. Items carry tags as names; tags are created when first given to an item.

item_count.description: Number of items (not in the trash) with this tag.

TargetRequest.description: A new comment state for a target. Omitted fields stay as they are.

closes_at.description: Close by itself from then on; `null` removes it.

hidden.description: `true` hides every comment of the target from everyone (and closes it).

TermFields.description: The name of a term in one language, and its parent. Omitted fields stay as they are.

locale.description:
The language of `name`, `slug`, `description` and the meta fields; omitted: the
default language. Needed to change those fields.

parent_id.description: Parent category (categories only); `null` moves it to the top.

slug.description: Omitted or empty: made from the name.

TermName.description: The name of a term in one language.

slug.description: Unique among the terms of the same taxonomy and language.

TermResponse.description: A category or tag, with its names in every language.

parent_id.description: Parent category; `null` at the top (always for tags).

TestRequest.description: Where to send a test mail.

replies.description:
The first shown replies, oldest first (at most `replies_limit`); get the rest from
`GET /api/v1/comments/public/comments/{id}/replies`.

ThreadComment.description: A top-level comment with its first replies.

access_token.description: Send this with every request: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

expires_in.description: Seconds until `access_token` expires. Refresh shortly before then.

refresh_token.description:
Exchange this for a new pair at `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`. Each refresh
token works once: always keep only the newest one. Store it securely.

refresh_token_expires_at.description: When `refresh_token` expires; after that, sign in again.

session_id.description:
The session these tokens belong to. It stays the same across refreshes; keep it
to recognize this client in `GET /api/v1/auth/me/sessions`.

TotpSetupResponse.description: What to enter in the authenticator app.

otpauth_url.description: The same secret as an `otpauth://` URI: show it as a QR code to scan.

secret.description: The secret, base32, for typing by hand.

locale.description: One of the languages of `AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_LOCALES`, other than the entry's.

allOf.description: Fields of the translation; omitted ones are copied from the entry.

error_code.description:
Why it failed, e.g. `content.translation_conflict` (someone changed the translation
meanwhile; it was not overwritten), `content.translation_invalid`, `ai.refused`,
`ai.output_truncated`, `ai.misconfigured`, `content.translation_canceled`.

result_entry_id.description:
The translation's draft, once `succeeded`. It is never published automatically and is
marked `ai_generated`.

source_revision_id.description: The revision of the source that is translated (its content when the request was made).

target_entry_id.description:
The translation that existed when the request was made and will be updated; `null`: a new
translation is created.

all.description: Stop mails about every comment followed with this address, not just this one.

token.description: The `token` of the link in a reply mail.

UnsubscribeResponse.description: The answer to an unsubscription: always the same.

UpdateCampaignRequest.description: Changes to a draft or scheduled campaign. Omitted fields stay as they are.

body_html.description:
Not sanitised: admin interfaces must preview it only inside a sandboxed
`<iframe sandbox>`. `null` removes it.

UpdateEndpointRequest.description: Changes to an endpoint. Omitted fields stay as they are.

disabled.description: `true` stops sending to it (pending retries are dropped); `false` starts again.

save_revision.description:
Keep a revision of the draft after this change (one is also kept automatically when
the last one is more than 10 minutes old).

UpdateEntryRequest.description: Changes to the draft of an entry.

UpdateFolderRequest.description: Changes to a folder. Omitted fields stay as they are.

parent_id.description: Move into this folder; `null` moves to the root. Not into itself or its subfolders.

UpdateFormRequest.description: Changes to a form. Omitted fields stay as they are; `null` clears the nullable ones.

fields.description:
The whole new list of fields; a change makes a new `version`. Old submissions keep
the labels of their own version.

notify_emails.description:
The whole new list of addresses mailed for each new submission (the mails carry the
answers). Changing it also needs the permission `forms.read`.

UpdateItemRequest.description: Changes to a media item. Omitted fields stay as they are.

alt.description: Text alternative, up to 1000 characters; `""` clears it.

caption.description: Caption, up to 2000 characters; `""` clears it.

folder_id.description: Move to this folder; `null` moves to the root.

name.description: New file name, 1 to 255 characters, without `/` or `\`.

tags.description:
Replace the tags of the item (each 1 to 50 characters, without `,`; at most 20);
`[]` removes them all. New tag names are created.

title.description: Title, up to 255 characters; `""` clears it.

oneOf.description: `public` lets anyone load the content without signing in.

UpdateListRequest.description: Changes to a list. Omitted fields stay as they are.

oneOf.description: `null`: posts in any language.
Setting `send` also needs the permission `newsletter.send`.

UpdateSubmissionRequest.description: A new status for a submission.

UpdateSubscriberRequest.description: Changes to a subscriber. Omitted fields stay as they are.

attributes.description: Replaces the attributes; up to 16 KiB of JSON.

oneOf.description: `blocked`: no mail at all, whatever the subscriptions.

unsubscribe_list_ids.description:
Unsubscribe from these lists (an admin cannot subscribe someone without consent; use
the import with a consent source).

UpdateUserRequest.description: Changes to an account. Omitted fields stay as they are.

disabled.description: `true` disables the account and signs it out everywhere; `false` enables it.

duplicates.description:
Items (not in the trash) whose content has the same SHA-256, oldest first, at most
20. Empty when the content is new. The upload is kept either way: delete it if you
would rather reuse one of these.

UploadedResponse.description: The uploaded item, plus the items already in the library with exactly the same content.

UserResponse.description: A user account. Never includes the password.

disabled_at.description:
When the account was disabled; `null` while it is active. A disabled account
cannot sign in or use its tokens.

email.description: Normalized email: lower case, no surrounding spaces. Unique.

email_verified_at.description:
When the owner confirmed `email` through a verification mail; `null` while it
is not verified.

UserRolesRequest.description: The complete list of roles a user should have.

role_ids.description: Ids of the roles. Replaces every role the user had; `[]` removes all.

VariantResponse.description: A smaller copy of an image.

url.description: Where to load it: the item's `url` with `&w=<width>`.

VerificationConfirmation.description: The token from a verification mail.

VerifiedResponse.description: The answer to an address confirmation.

Visibility.description: Who may load the content without signing in.

bearer.description: A short-lived access token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
